Hi X!  Good to hear from you!

A couple of thoughts..


On Fri, Mar 7, 2014 at 1:06 PM, X wrote:
Hi Nick! How is it going?
I've been working with the BioGeoBEARS package in two ways: 1) by
adapting the out-of-the-box Psychotria wiki example to my data, and 2)
by running bears_2param_(...). In the first case, I recover two dozen
possible areas, and hence meaningless results. In the second case, I
just get a diversity of errors.

 
bears_2param...etc. are old functions that I am no longer supporting, they will be cut from the next version, the bears_optim_run function with the settings specified in the BioGeoBEARS_run_object is the One True Path now...

 

I don't wanna overwhelm you, so I will start by asking a single question.

In my dataset, I have a single species that occur in 4 areas.
BioGeoBEARS won't let me have a max_range_size smaller than 4 (it
errors if I try). I imagine that this is why I recover so many
possible ancestral areas for some of the deeper nodes (pies with two
dozen colors).

A coupla things:

1. First, each slice is a range/state rather than an area.  It could be that the ranges are fairly similar to each other, e.g.

ABC
BC
AC
...etc...it is possible to have low confidence about the exact range, but high confidence that, say, area C was occupied.

You can extract the exact ancestral probabilities of each state with e.g.:

resDEC$ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_top_AT_node

See: 
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/biogeobears/1wyy3jV2gDs


2. But, second, it is common to get high uncertainty in ancestral nodes under DEC, if it poorly fits the data.  You may find improvements under e.g. DEC+J, if it happens to fit better.



On this:

> However, when running DEC on RASP, I am able to set the 'Maximum areas
> at each to node' to smaller values (e.g., 2). Results are then much
> more resolved.
> 
> Question is: can I do the same in BioGeoBEARS? That is, can I limit
> the number of areas at each node to a value smaller than maximum
> number of areas observed for the sampled taxa?
> 


It shouldn't be possible to have a maximum range size smaller than an observed range size. It would be like having a DNA model that only allowed 3 states, A, C, and, G, but then having data that had states ACGT.  The probability calculations involve a transition matrix where the rows are ancestral states, and the columns are descendent states, so if you have a tip with range ABCD, that had better be a possible descendant state in the transition matrix.

I can't imagine what RASP is doing, it would either be Really Bad (e.g. arbitrary truncation of a geographic range from ABCD to AB), or it has some model where "ABCD could mean the ancestor was either AB or BC or CD or AC or AD" and code that into the likelihood calculations. Hopefully that would be described somewhere though!  The versions of LAGRANGE definitely do not allow a maximum range size smaller than an observed range size.

Cheers!  Let me know if you want to join the BioGeoBEARS google group!
Nick
